title: Give the fixture's rows random-looking UUIDs
description: The submission fixture's rows have hand-numbered UUIDs such as 00000006-0000-4000-8000-000000000006, so their SlugModel slugs come out as S00000006 instead of looking like real ones, such as S3f2a9c1e. Give every row a fixed but random-looking UUID4 and recompute the slugs.
acceptance_criteria: Tests: every fixture submission's slug is make_slug('S', its UUID); no slug is hand-numbered (S0000...). just ci passes.
close_reason: Remapped every fixture row to a fixed random-looking UUID4 (derived from its old ID) and recomputed the slugs, on the fixture's own branch, and cascaded the change up the stack. The records test now compares in local ID order, since pk order no longer follows the content.

title: Accept API bodies over Django's 2.5 MB limit
description: Django rejects request bodies over DATA_UPLOAD_MAX_MEMORY_SIZE, 2.5 MB by default, with a 400 before the CSS sees them. A germline record is about 600 bytes with a one-line comment, so 10,000 records, ClinVar's maximum, is at least 6 MB, and VCI comments are paragraphs. Raise the limit enough for 10,000 records with long comments (measure a realistic VCI record), or lift it for the submissions endpoint only. Caddy sets no body limit, so only Django needs changing.
acceptance_criteria: Tests: a POST of 10,000 records with realistic comments is saved (201); a body over the new limit is rejected. just ci passes.
close_reason: Raised DATA_UPLOAD_MAX_MEMORY_SIZE to 64 MB, enough for 10,000 records with ~6 KB comments, and added Caddy request_body limits: 64MB for /css/api/v1/submissions, 2.5MB for every other path. The Caddyfile change wasn't run through caddy validate locally (Caddy isn't installed); check it on tools-test.

title: Add fixtures for CSS and ClinVar submissions
description: Add a Django fixture, fixtures/test_submissions.json, with a VCI API key and submissions in every status, each with one to three records: received and send_failed ones the CSS has but ClinVar never got, and submitted, processing, processed, and error ones forwarded to ClinVar, with ClinVar IDs, responses, and summary reports with SCVs and errors where ClinVar would have them. Add a just recipe to load it, like the HCI's django-loaddata-test, so the pages can be built against it.
acceptance_criteria: Tests: the fixture loads; it has a submission in every status; every forwarded one has a ClinVar ID and none of the others do; each submission's Record rows match what parsing its payload gives. just ci passes. The README and docs/how-to.md say how to load it.
close_reason: Added fixtures/test_submissions.json (a VCI key and six submissions, one per status, ten records) generated from make_record and record_fields, a just django-loaddata-test recipe, and tests that the fixture covers every status, its records match its payloads, and every page renders.

title: Validate the API body and save its records
description: Replace POST /css/api/v1/submissions's untyped body with Ninja schemas for ClinVar's germline content (germlineSubmission, 1 to 10,000 records, plus assertionCriteria, behalfOrgID, and clinvarSubmissionReleaseStatus), using ClinVar's camelCase names as aliases and forbidding fields we don't model. Save the submission's fields and its Record rows in one transaction with the payload, then forward the payload as sent. Put the parsing in a function the fixtures' tests can reuse. This replaces count_records and fixes its undercount of germlineSubmission records. Move the test fixtures to germlineSubmission.
acceptance_criteria: Tests: a valid body saves the submission's fields and one Record per record; a body with an unknown field, a bad classification, or more than 10,000 records gets 422 and saves nothing; the payload is forwarded unchanged; the OpenAPI docs list the fields. just ci passes.
close_reason: POST /submissions now validates the body against content.Content (germline records only, extra fields forbidden) and saves the submission's fields and Records in one transaction; the payload is saved and forwarded as sent. Replaces count_records. Found that Django's 2.5 MB body limit is below a full submission; filed separately.

title: Add the Record model for a submission's records
description: Add a Record model, one ClinVar germline record in a submission, with a foreign key to Submission (related_name records). Fields: record status (novel or update), ClinVar accession (SCV), local ID, local key, submitted assembly, HGVS, gene symbol, condition db and ID, classification, mode of inheritance, date last evaluated, comment, allele origin, affected status, and collection method, each with ClinVar's allowed values as choices. Add the submission-level fields to Submission: assertion criteria db and ID, behalf org ID, and release status. Keep history on Record. Show records as a read-only inline on the submission's admin page.
acceptance_criteria: Tests: a record belongs to a submission and is ordered by local ID; its choices match ClinVar's terms; its history is kept; the submission's admin page lists its records. just ci passes. The README describes the model.
close_reason: Added Record with ClinVar's germline fields and terms as choices, the submission-level content fields, history, and a read-only admin inline. Citations aren't modeled yet.

title: Store ClinVar records as fields
description: The CSS stores each submission's payload only as a JSON blob. Staff pages, search, and grouping by affiliation need the classification's fields (variant, condition, classification, inheritance, dates) in columns. Store them in models alongside the payload, validate the API body against the shape we model, and add fixtures with submissions in every status so the pages can be built and tested.
design: Scope: germline variant classifications from the VCI, ClinVar's germlineSubmission records. The payload stays stored and forwarded exactly as the client sent it; the fields are a parsed copy. The API's body schema forbids fields we don't model, so the fields always hold everything we forward. Each record is one variant-condition pair, so a record has one HGVS variant, one condition, and one observedIn; ClinVar allows more, but the VCI never sends more. The classification choices are the five ACMG terms the VCI uses; mode of inheritance and the other enums use ClinVar's full lists. Records extend UUIDModel, not SlugModel: staff find them by their localID or SCV, not by a CSS ID.
notes: 2026-10-20: Liam wants to see VCI submissions in the local app using dummy fixture data only, not real VCI data. The AS port isn't needed for this: the VCI sends the affiliation's name with its ID.

title: Count germlineSubmission records in the 10,000 limit
description: count_records in clinvar_submission_service/services.py counts only clinvarSubmission and clinvarDeletion. ClinVar's current schema puts germline records in germlineSubmission (with germlineClassification), and also has noClassificationSubmission, oncogenicitySubmission, and clinicalImpactSubmission; clinvarSubmission is the older shape that uses clinicalSignificance. The VCI will send germlineSubmission, so a payload of any size passes our 10,000-record check and ClinVar rejects it instead. Count every top-level submission array. Update the test fixtures in test_api.py, test_clients.py, and test_contract.py to use germlineSubmission so they match what clients send.
acceptance_criteria: Tests: count_records counts germlineSubmission, noClassificationSubmission, oncogenicitySubmission, clinicalImpactSubmission, clinvarSubmission, and clinvarDeletion records; POST /css/api/v1/submissions with 10,001 germlineSubmission records returns 422. Fixtures use germlineSubmission. just ci passes.

title: Create the server .env during init
description:
Server initialization fails at the "Migrate the database" task. The init playbook runs manage.py (migrate, then collectstatic) right after it clones the repo, and manage.py loads its settings from the .env file in the root of the repository. On a fresh server there is no .env yet, so DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE is unset and Django cannot load its settings. Today the only fix is to SSH in, write .env by hand, and rerun init.

Add a task to the init playbook, after the project is installed and before anything runs manage.py, that creates .env from .env.example when the file does not exist. Fill in only the values needed to boot on a server: DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE=config.settings.prod, ENV, SUBDOMAIN (from the inventory's subdomain variable), and a newly generated SECRET_KEY, since the production settings refuse to start without one. Leave the other keys empty, so secrets (Clerk, Sentry, backup and other service credentials) are still entered by hand afterward. The task must never overwrite an existing .env, because it holds secrets entered by hand; rerunning init on a set-up server should leave .env untouched. Make the file readable only by the ubuntu user (mode 0600).

Update How to Set Up a Server for the First Time in docs/how-to.md to say init creates .env, and which keys still have to be filled in by hand before the first deploy.
acceptance_criteria:
- On a server with no .env, the init playbook creates one with DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE, ENV, SUBDOMAIN, and a generated SECRET_KEY set, and init runs past migrate and collectstatic.
- Rerunning init on a server that already has a .env leaves the file unchanged (the task reports ok, not changed).
- The created .env has the same keys as .env.example (just env-check would report no differences) and mode 0600.
- just infra-all passes.
- docs/how-to.md describes the new step and the keys left to fill in by hand.

title: Use ClinVar's wording for statuses, with tooltips
description: The CSS's status tags use made-up wording (Sent, ClinVar Is Checking, Accepted, Has Errors), which staff confused. Use ClinVar's words for the statuses ClinVar reports: Submitted, Processing, Processed, and Error, and for each record's result, ClinVar's per-record processingStatus, Success or Error. The CSS's own statuses become Not Sent (was Not Sent Yet) and Send Failed (was Not Sent). Give every status a tooltip, using common/tooltip.html, that explains it in plain words close to ClinVar's Submission API docs; an Error's tooltip says whether some or all records failed, from ClinVar's errorCode 1 or 2. Apply the same wording to the detail page's explanation, the affiliations page's column headers, and the list's filter toggles.
acceptance_criteria: Tests: each status's tag shows its new label and its tooltip text; an Error's tooltip differs for errorCode 1 and 2; record results say Success or Error; the affiliations headers use the new words; no page shows the old labels.

title: Name submission statuses relative to ClinVar
description: Submission.Status values such as received and submitted don't say which tool they're relative to; submitted could mean submitted to the CSS. Rename every value so it names ClinVar: not_sent_to_clinvar (was received), send_to_clinvar_failed (was send_failed), submitted_to_clinvar, processing_at_clinvar, processed_by_clinvar, and error_at_clinvar. The last four mirror ClinVar's own status values (submitted, processing, processed, error) from its Submission API docs, so the poller keeps mapping ClinVar's strings onto them. Migrate existing rows and their history, and update the fixtures, the API, and the docs. Nothing is deployed yet, so the API's status values can change.
acceptance_criteria: Tests: a migration test (or the migrations-up-to-date check) covers the new choices; the poller maps each ClinVar status to its renamed value; the API returns the new values; existing model, view, polling, fixture, and API tests pass with the new names.
close_reason: Statuses are now not_sent_to_clinvar, send_to_clinvar_failed, submitted_to_clinvar, processing_at_clinvar, processed_by_clinvar, and error_at_clinvar; migration 0005 renames existing rows and history.

title: Port the HCI's tooltip template
description: The CSS's status tags need tooltips, and the HCI already has a tooltip pattern: common/tooltip.html renders an icon with a Tippy.js tooltip and no visible text, and tooltips.js attaches Tippy to every [data-tippy-content] element, including ones HTMX swaps in. Port it into the shared common app and the base layout: add @popperjs/core and tippy.js to package.json, copy them (with source maps and tippy.css) in build.js, and add tooltips.js.
acceptance_criteria: Tests: the base layout loads Popper, Tippy, and tooltips.js; common/tooltip.html renders the text in data-tippy-content and an is-sr-only span, the icon is focusable, and no text sits beside it.
close_reason: Ported common/tooltip.html, tooltips.js, and Tippy.js with Popper from the HCI.

title: Render the submissions list with django-tables2
description: The CSS submissions list is a hand-written table and a search form with a Search button. Match the HCI: render the table with django-tables2 (sortable columns, the HCI's Bulma tables.html template and pagination), and use the HCI's search input, which searches as you type with htmx and swaps in only the results. The sent= and affiliation= filters and the q= search stay in the view, so they keep working; sorting and paging links keep the other query parameters, and the live search sends the active filters along. Label the Received column as received by the CSS, since it's when the CSS got the submission, not ClinVar.
acceptance_criteria: Tests: sorting by a column orders the rows; paging keeps q, sent, and affiliation; an HX-Request gets only the results partial; the search input carries the sent and affiliation filters; existing filter and search tests still pass.
close_reason: The submissions list is a django-tables2 table with the HCI's live search; filters stay in the view and carry through sorting, paging, and search.

title: Put the submission tab before Affiliations
description: On a submission's page, the CSS header shows its tab after Submissions and Affiliations. The user wants it right after Submissions, since a submission is opened from that list.
acceptance_criteria: The header lists Submissions, then the open submission's tab, then Affiliations. A view test checks the order on the detail page.
close_reason: The submission's tab now sits between Submissions and Affiliations.

title: Accept the affiliation with each submission
description: The VCI forwards each submission's affiliation, the curation group whose classifications it holds, along with the ClinVar content, so the CSS can group submissions by it. ClinVar's content has no place for it, so change POST /css/api/v1/submissions's body to an envelope: {"affiliation": {"id": 10007, "name": "Hearing Loss VCEP"}, "content": {...ClinVar content...}}. The ID is the AS's integer affiliation ID, and the name is the one the VCI already reads from the AS's API, so the CSS can show names without the AS (the tools don't share domain data). Store both on Submission (the ID indexed), keep payload as the content alone, which is still what's forwarded, and return the affiliation from the GET endpoints. The API isn't deployed yet, so change v1 rather than adding v2. Regenerate the fixtures so submissions belong to at least three affiliations.
acceptance_criteria: Tests: a POST with an affiliation saves its ID and name and forwards only the content; a POST without one, or with a non-integer ID or empty name, gets 422 and saves nothing; GET returns the affiliation; the fixture has submissions from at least three affiliations and its records still match its payloads. just ci passes. docs/design.md's API section shows the envelope.
close_reason: POST /submissions now takes {affiliation: {id, name}, content}; Submission stores affiliation_id (indexed) and affiliation_name, payload is the content alone, and GET returns the affiliation. Fixtures now have eight submissions from five made-up affiliations.

title: Save each record's ClinVar result on its Record
description: When the poller stores a summary report, copy each record's processingStatus, SCV accession, and errors onto the Record it matches by local ID, so pages and search can use them without reading the report's JSON.

title: Group submissions by affiliation
description: Group the staff pages' submissions by affiliation, using the affiliation ID and name the VCI sends with each submission: a filter by affiliation on the list, and each affiliation's counts of submissions waiting, sent, and with errors.
acceptance_criteria: Tests: the list can be filtered to one affiliation; the affiliation summary counts each affiliation's submissions correctly against the fixtures; an unknown affiliation filter shows nothing rather than everything. just ci passes.
close_reason: Added an Affiliations tab that counts each affiliation's submissions (not sent, ClinVar checking, accepted, errors, total), named from its newest submission, and an affiliation= filter on the list that combines with the sent filter; an unknown or non-numeric ID shows nothing.

title: Where does a submission's affiliation come from?
description: Staff want submissions grouped by curation group (affiliation). ClinVar's content has no affiliation, only behalfOrgID, a ClinVar organization ID. Options: (1) the client sends the affiliation ID next to the content, which changes the API body to an envelope such as {"affiliation": "10007", "content": {...}}; (2) the CSS looks the affiliation up from behalfOrgID, which needs each affiliation's ClinVar organization ID, likely stored in the AS; (3) both, checking they agree. Which one?
close_reason: Decided (Liam, 2026-10-20): the VCI forwards the affiliation with each submission. The CSS doesn't derive it from behalfOrgID or look it up in the AS.

title: Show CSS and ClinVar submissions on the staff pages
description: Use the Record fields on the staff pages: list submissions the CSS has but ClinVar never got separately from ones forwarded to ClinVar, and show each record's variant, condition, classification, and inheritance in plain language. Build and test against the fixtures.
close_reason: List page: affiliation and genes columns, an All / Not Sent to ClinVar / Sent to ClinVar filter (sent=), and search by ID, ClinVar ID, affiliation, gene, or HGVS. Detail page: affiliation, and a records table from Record (variant, condition, classification, inheritance, last evaluated, new or update) with ClinVar's result and SCV matched from the summary report by local ID. Conditions show MONDO IDs, not names: the CSS has no condition names.

title: Get the ClinVar service account and API key
description: The CSS needs a ClinVar Submission API key belonging to ClinGen's organization's service account, and we need to know which organization submits. Liam doesn't have one yet. Ask clinvar@ncbi.nlm.nih.gov for a service account for the Submission API if ClinGen has none. Until then, CSS_CLINVAR_API_KEY stays empty, so every submission ends in send_failed. Record the organization and where the key is stored when this is answered.

title: Add the submission pages
description: Behind has_css_permissions, add a submissions list (newest first, with slug, client, status tag, ClinVar ID, added date) and a detail page (status, client, ClinVar ID, payload, ClinVar's latest response and summary report, and error message) with tabs like the ETS. A send_failed submission's page has a Resend button (POST, confirm) that reuses the API's forward-and-record function. Status tags follow the color key: grey received/submitted/processing, red send_failed/error, green processed. Use plain language; raw responses are shown as formatted JSON for staff who need them, errors stay plain.
acceptance_criteria: Tests first: pages need the permission; list and detail render; Resend only for send_failed and records the new attempt; each status gets the right tag color; header tabs active state. READMEs updated; just ci passes.
notes:
Follow the HCI and common: a list built on common's search list view and a django-tables2 table (slug, status, ClinVar ID, client, added, updated; search by slug and ClinVar ID) with HTMX live search; a detail page; history and change pages built on common's history helpers. When the summary report exists, show each record's processingStatus and SCV (clinvarAccession). Add Submission.get_absolute_url here. Resend records who resent it through simple-history's history_user. Tests: Resend shows only for send_failed, a successful resend sets the ClinVar ID and submitted, a failed one keeps send_failed with the new message, resending anything else is rejected, users without permission get 403, the list returns the partial for HX-Request.
Decision while working (2026-10-17): this repo's common app has no search list view, django-tables2 tables, or history views, and adding them would be shared code outside a css bead. So the pages follow the ETS instead: a plain list with a GET search by slug or ClinVar ID and Django pagination, and a detail page. Change history stays in the Django admin. Following the plain-language rule for non-technical staff, the pages don't show raw JSON or ClinVar's raw error text. They describe the status in words and list each record's result and SCV from the summary report; the payload and responses are in the admin. The CSS's home page is the submission list.
close_reason: Added the submission list (search, pagination) as the CSS home page, the detail page with plain-language status and per-record results, the status tag partial in the color key, and the POST-only Resend view through forward_submission. History stays in the admin; see the bead's notes.

title: Run poll_clinvar as a systemd service
description: Add a systemd unit template for the poller next to gunicorn.service in infra/ansible/tasks/placement, placed and enabled by the init playbook, and restarted by the deploy playbook after Gunicorn. It runs uv run src/manage.py poll_clinvar as the same user with the same .env and restarts on failure.
acceptance_criteria: The unit is placed, enabled, and restarted by Ansible; just infra-all passes; infra docs and docs/how-to.md mention the poller service.
close_reason: Added poll-clinvar.service (restart on failure, SIGTERM with a 120-second stop timeout), placed and started by init.yml and placed and restarted by deploy.yml after Gunicorn. how-to.md covers checking on it.

title: Add the poll_clinvar management command
description: Add management/commands/poll_clinvar.py. Each pass takes a small batch from Submission.objects.due_to_poll(), calls get_status for each, stores latest_response, clinvar_updated_at, last_polled_at, maps ClinVar's status to processing, processed, or error (with clinvar_error_code), downloads the summary report on a final status, and otherwise pushes next_poll_at out with exponential backoff up to a maximum. On a ClinVar error it backs off; on 429 it waits at least Retry-After. Errors for one submission are logged with its slug and reported to Sentry, and don't stop the loop. It sleeps between passes, supports --once for tests, and exits cleanly on SIGTERM after the current submission.
acceptance_criteria: Tests first with FakeClinVarClient and --once: each status transition; summary report stored on final status; backoff grows and caps; Retry-After honored; one failing submission doesn't block others; SIGTERM handler stops the loop. READMEs updated; just ci passes.
notes: Poll only submitted and processing (due_to_poll), never send_failed or anything without a ClinVar ID. Map actions[0].status straight onto ours. Default interval in minutes with backoff up to hours; put interval, batch size, and backoff limits in settings. Tests: a 429 sets next_poll_at at least Retry-After seconds out; a failed summary-report download is retried next pass without changing the status; send_failed is never polled or resent. Add a just recipe to run it locally.
close_reason: Added polling.Poller (batches of due submissions, oldest first; doubling backoff capped by settings; Retry-After; summary report on final status; per-submission errors logged and sent to Sentry) and the poll_clinvar command with --once and a SIGTERM handler, plus just django-poll-clinvar.

title: Add the versioned submissions API
description: Add django-ninja and a NinjaAPI mounted at /css/v1/api/ with the API-key auth. POST /submissions saves a received Submission owned by the key, forwards it with ClinVarClient, and sets submitted with the SUB ID and next_poll_at, or send_failed with an error message (including when the client isn't configured); it returns the slug and status. GET /submissions/{slug} returns status, ClinVar ID, latest response, and summary report for the caller's own submission (404 otherwise). GET /submissions lists the caller's submissions, newest first, paginated. Put the forward-and-record logic in a function the staff resend view can reuse.
acceptance_criteria: Tests first with FakeClinVarClient: create succeeds; ClinVar failure and unconfigured client give send_failed; missing or bad key is 401; a client can't read another's submission; list is scoped and paginated; OpenAPI docs render at /css/v1/api/docs. READMEs and design.md updated; just ci passes.
notes:
The POST body is the ClinVar submission content object; validate that it's a JSON object with at most 10,000 records and return 422 otherwise. The CSS adds the actions/AddData envelope. A failed POST is never retried automatically: set send_failed, store the message, and return the slug with send_failed. Put save-and-forward in one function (e.g. services.forward_submission) that the Resend view also calls. Tests: unknown, inactive, and missing keys get 401; invalid bodies get 422; a failed POST isn't retried.
Decision (2026-10-17): the API moved from /css/v1/api/ to /css/api/v1/, the more common order, so everything under /css/api/ is the API whatever its version.
close_reason: Added the v1 Ninja API at /css/v1/api/ (create, list paginated, read) behind ApiKeyAuth, scoped to the caller's key, and services.forward_submission for the API and the Resend button. Over 10,000 records gets a 422; an unconfigured ClinVar key gives send_failed.

title: Add API keys for CSS clients
description: Add an ApiKey model (UUIDModel, with history): a client name, a hashed key (store only a hash, e.g. SHA-256 of a random token), a short non-secret prefix to identify it, active flag, added_at, last_used_at. Staff create keys in the admin, which shows the raw key once on creation and never again. Add a Ninja APIKeyHeader auth class (header X-API-Key) that accepts active keys and sets request.auth to the ApiKey. Add an api_key foreign key from Submission (PROTECT, nullable for admin-made rows).
acceptance_criteria: Tests first: a key verifies by hash and the raw key isn't stored; inactive or unknown keys are rejected; last_used_at updates; admin creation shows the key once. READMEs updated; just ci passes.
notes: The standalone AS planned the same ApiKey model and auth. It lives in the CSS app for now since the CSS is its only user; when the AS needs one, move it to a shared app so both tools use it, keeping a key tied to one tool.
close_reason: Added ApiKey (SHA-256 hash and prefix only, active flag, last_used_at), ApiKeyAuth on the X-API-Key header, the admin that shows a new key once, and Submission.api_key. Added django-ninja here for APIKeyHeader.

title: Add the ClinVar Submission API client
description: Add clients.py with a ClinVarClient built on requests: submit(payload) POSTs the AddData envelope and returns the SUB ID; get_status(clinvar_id) GETs the actions endpoint and returns a parsed status (ClinVar status, updated timestamp, errorCode, summary report URL, raw response); get_summary_report(url) downloads the report. It sends SP-API-KEY, uses a request timeout, raises a typed error on non-2xx or network failure (carrying Retry-After for 429), and never logs the key. from_settings() reads CSS_CLINVAR_API_KEY and CSS_CLINVAR_API_URL (default the apitest base) and raises ImproperlyConfigured when the key is empty. Add fakes.py with an in-memory FakeClinVarClient for other beads' tests. Add the settings and .env.example keys.
acceptance_criteria: Tests first with mocked requests: envelope and header shape, SUB ID parsing, status parsing for each ClinVar status, 429 Retry-After, timeouts and 5xx raise the typed error, missing key raises ImproperlyConfigured, key never appears in logs. Settings test for the default URL. READMEs updated; just ci passes.
notes: From the ClinVar API spike (see the epic's notes for response formats): send Content-Type: application/json too. Parse the SUB ID from {"id": ...} on 200 or 201, and treat 204 as a successful dry run. Read status from actions[0].status, ClinVar's updated timestamp from actions[0].updated, errorCode from actions[0].responses[0].message.errorCode, and the summary report URL from actions[0].responses[0].files[0].url. The report download also sends SP-API-KEY. Timeouts, 5xx, and 429 are retryable (carry Retry-After on 429); 400 and 401 aren't, and keep ClinVar's message. Prod settings must use the production URL; test settings must not. Add contract tests skipped unless RUN_CONTRACT_TESTS=1 and a key is set: the POST uses ?dry-run=true (expect 204), status reads use apitest. They never create a production submission.
close_reason: Added ClinVarClient (submit with dry run, get_status, get_summary_report) with retryable ClinVarError and Retry-After, FakeClinVarClient, skipped-by-default contract test, and CSS_CLINVAR_API_URL/KEY settings defaulting to apitest.

title: Add the CSS app with the Submission model and admin
description: Create src/clinvar_submission_service/ (verbose name ClinVar Submission Service), mounted at /css/ with namespace css and an index page behind a new has_css_permissions flag on auth_.UserProfile (with migration). Add Submission, ported from the standalone CSS: extends SlugModel with prefix S; payload (JSON), clinvar_submission_id, status (the epic's six statuses, default received), clinvar_updated_at, clinvar_error_code, latest_response, summary_report, error_message, added_at, updated_at, last_polled_at, next_poll_at, and history. A manager method due_to_poll() returns submitted or processing submissions whose next_poll_at has passed. Register it in the admin with ClinVar's fields read-only. The API-key owner is added later by the API-key bead.
acceptance_criteria: Tests first: slug is S plus 8 hex chars; new submission is received; history records a status change; due_to_poll returns only due submitted/processing submissions; admin list and change pages render; index needs has_css_permissions; landing page links to the CSS. New app README, docs.json entry, auth_ README updated; just ci passes.
close_reason: Added clinvar_submission_service at /css/ with Submission (SlugModel, prefix S) and its admin, ported from the standalone CSS's unmerged model; added has_css_permissions with a migration and a profile row.

title: Carry the CSS's design into docs/design.md
description: docs/design.md says the CSS's domain design carries over from its standalone repository, but that repository is being deleted. Add a 'The ClinVar Submission Service' section, like the ETS's, that records the epic's design: what the CSS does, the ClinVar Submission API calls, the submission lifecycle (save first, forward, submitted or send_failed, staff resend, poll to a final status, summary report), the statuses as a bulleted list with whether each is final, the API at /css/v1/api/ and its endpoints and API-key auth, the poller's loop, backoff, and Retry-After handling, ClinVar outside production (apitest everywhere but prod), and secrets. Update the URL Layout section to /css/v1/api/ and Key Libraries with requests. Don't mention past architectures. Don't add an open-questions section; the missing service account is a decision bead.
acceptance_criteria: design.md has the CSS section and the /css/v1/api/ prefix; no mention of Rust or other past architectures; no tables; prose wrapped at 88 characters; just ci passes.

title: Port the ClinVar Submission Service
description: Bring the CSS's design and its Submission model over from the standalone clinvar-submission-service repository, which is being deleted, and build the rest of the CSS here: the ClinVar client, API keys, the versioned submissions API, the poller and its systemd service, and the staff pages.
design:
The CSS accepts ClinVar submissions from ClinGen client systems through an authenticated JSON API, forwards them to the NCBI ClinVar Submission API, polls ClinVar until each one reaches a final status, and shows staff every submission in a small web UI. It was designed in a standalone repository that is being deleted; only its design and an unmerged Submission model existed there. This epic brings that design into docs/design.md and builds the CSS as src/clinvar_submission_service/, mounted at /css/ with the URL namespace css.

Decisions already made:

- Don't mention past architectures (such as a Rust prototype) anywhere.
- The API is a Django Ninja NinjaAPI mounted at /css/api/v1/, so a future breaking change can live at /css/api/v2/. OpenAPI docs at /css/api/v1/docs.
- Submission extends common.models.SlugModel with slug prefix S (S3f2a9c1e), not a zero-padded integer slug.
- Statuses: received (saved, not yet sent; not final), send_failed (the POST to ClinVar never succeeded, so there's no ClinVar ID; final; staff can resend), submitted (ClinVar has it, not validating yet; not final), processing (ClinVar is validating; not final), processed (every record succeeded; final), error (ClinVar reported record errors: errorCode 1 is some records, 2 is every record; final). send_failed and error stay separate.
- The CSS saves the Submission before forwarding it, so every request is recorded even if ClinVar never got it. It never resends on its own; staff resend send_failed submissions from the UI.
- ClinVar API (https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/clinvar/docs/api_http/): every request sends the service account's key in the SP-API-KEY header. POST {base}/submissions/ with body {"actions": [{"type": "AddData", "targetDb": "clinvar", "data": {"content": <payload>}}]} returns {"id": "SUB999999"}. GET {base}/submissions/SUB999999/actions/ returns the status; once processing finishes, the response links to a JSON summary report. Production base: https://submit.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/api/v1. Test base: https://submit.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/apitest/v1, which validates fully but never makes data public. Only production uses the production base; dev, tests, and tools-test use apitest. Unit tests use a fake client and send no requests.
- Clients authenticate to the CSS API with an API key in a header. Keys are hashed at rest, managed in the Django admin, and belong to the CSS only. A client sees only its own submissions. Clients poll GET for status; there are no webhooks.
- poll_clinvar is a long-running management command run by its own systemd service next to Gunicorn. It keeps its state in the database (next_poll_at), backs off exponentially up to a maximum, honors Retry-After on 429, polls on a scale of minutes, and exits cleanly on SIGTERM.
- Never log the NCBI API key or client API keys.
- Staff UI pages are behind a new has_css_permissions flag on auth_.UserProfile; every approved user sees every submission. Plain language for non-technical staff.
- We don't have the ClinVar service account or API key yet, so everything must work with the key unset (the client raises ImproperlyConfigured and the API records send_failed).
notes:
# ClinVar Submission API findings (checked 2026-09-29)                      
                                                                            
Sources:                                                                    
                                                                            
• https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/clinvar/docs/api_http/ (main reference)      
• https://ncbiinsights.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/2026/03/02/update-clinvar-          
submission-api/ (March 2026: schema updated for functional data such as     
MAVEs; the endpoints didn't change)                                         
• Schemas: https://github.com/ncbi/clinvar/tree/master/submission_api_schema
(submission_api_schema.json for production, submission_apitest_schema.json  
for test; production last modified 2026-06-30)                              
                                                                            
Caveat: I read the docs through a summarizing fetch tool. Recheck exact     
field names against the page and the JSON schemas while building the client.
                                                                            
## Access                                                                   
                                                                            
• The submitting organization must already be registered with ClinVar and   
needs a service account. Request one by emailing clinvar@ncbi.nlm.nih.gov.  
• The API key is 64 alphanumeric characters, created in the Submission      
Portal under My Profile > Groups > API Access. It can't be recovered; if    
it's lost, create a new one.                                                
• Every request sends the header SP-API-KEY: <key>. Requests with a body    
also send Content-Type: application/json.                                   
                                                                            
## Base URLs                                                                
                                                                            
• Production: https://submit.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/api/v1/submissions/           
• Test: https://submit.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/apitest/v1/submissions/ runs full   
validation and returns SUB IDs and statuses like production, but its data   
"will never be made public in ClinVar, even if the response indicates that  
no errors were found."                                                      
• Dry run: add ?dry-run=true to a POST. It checks format and connectivity   
only and returns 204 without creating a submission.                         
                                                                            
## Create a submission                                                      
                                                                            
POST {base}/ with this body:                                                
{"actions": [{"type": "AddData", "targetDb": "clinvar", "data": {"content": 
{ ...ClinVar submission content... }}}]}                                    
                                                                            
• A submission can hold up to 10,000 records.                               
• System errors and basic schema validation come back immediately.          
Everything else is validated asynchronously.                                
• 200 or 201 returns {"id": "SUBnnnnnn"}; 204 means the dry run succeeded;  
400 returns {"message": "Submission is incorrect"}; 401 returns {"message": 
"No valid API key provided"}; 429 means wait the number of seconds in the   
Retry-After header and try again; 5xx is a server error.                    
• Updates: include "clinvarAccession" (the SCV) and "recordStatus": "update"
in the record. Deletions: a clinvarDeletion object with the accession and an
optional reason.                                                            
                                                                            
## Read status                                                              
                                                                            
GET {base}/SUBnnnnnn/actions/ (the test environment uses the apitest path). 
The HTTP codes are the same as for POST.                                    
{"actions": [{"id": "SUB999999-1", "targetDb": "clinvar", "status":         
"processing", "updated": "<ISO 8601 UTC>",                                  
"responses": [{"status": "...", "message": {"errorCode": null, "severity":  
"info", "text": "..."} | null,                                              
"files": [{"url": "https://submit.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/api/2.0/files/.../subNNN-
summary-report.json/"}],                                                    
"objects": [{"accession": null, "targetDb": "clinvar",                      
"content": {"clinvarProcessingStatus": "In processing",                     
"clinvarReleaseStatus": "Not released"}}]}]}]}                              
                                                                            
• The status is at actions[0].status:                                       
    • submitted: received and waiting to be validated                       
    • processing: being validated                                           
    • processed: every record in the batch succeeded (final)                
    • error: one or more records failed (final). message.errorCode 1 means  
    partial success; 2 means every record failed.                           
• When processing finishes, responses[0].files[0].url points to a JSON      
summary report: submissionName, submissionDate, batchProcessingStatus,      
batchReleaseStatus, totalCount, totalErrors, totalSuccess, totalPublic, and 
submissions[] with identifiers (localID, localKey, clinvarLocalKey,         
clinvarAccession, which is the SCV) and processingStatus for each record,   
plus error details for failed records.                                      
• Records that process successfully become public in the next weekly release,
usually Sunday night. The docs give no processing-time guarantee and no     
polling guidance.                                                           
• The docs give no rate-limit numbers, only the 429 response with Retry-    
After.

title: Move server secrets to AWS Secrets Manager
description:
The server's secrets live only in a hand-edited .env file on each server. They have no backup or history, rotating one means SSHing in, and setting up a new server means finding every value again. Move the important ones into AWS Secrets Manager, in the stanford-clingen-projects account, so a server's .env can be rebuilt from one place.

Store one secret per Terraform workspace (tools/test and tools/prod), as JSON key-value pairs named after the .env keys. Terraform creates each secret and an IAM policy for reading it, but not its values, so the values never land in Terraform state; staff enter them in the AWS console. Secrets to move: SECRET_KEY, CLERK_SECRET_KEY, SENTRY_DSN, the backup writer's AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID and AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, and the ETS's ETS_AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID and ETS_AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY. Values that aren't secret (DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE, ENV, SUBDOMAIN, SENTRY_ENV, bucket names) stay where they are.

How the server gets the values depends on the decision bead that blocks this one. This builds on tools-dd4, which creates .env during init; extend that work rather than adding a second way to write .env.

Update docs/how-to.md: how to add or change a secret, and how a server's .env gets its values.
acceptance_criteria:
- terraform validate passes, and terraform plan in each workspace shows the secret and its read policy, with no secret values in the plan or state.
- On a fresh server, init plus a deploy produces a working .env with every moved secret filled in, without hand-editing.
- Changing a value in Secrets Manager and following the documented steps updates the running app.
- just infra-all and just ci pass.
- docs/how-to.md covers adding, changing, and loading secrets.

title: Decide: read secrets from Secrets Manager at deploy time or run time?
description:
Moving the server's secrets to AWS Secrets Manager needs one decision first: where do the secrets get read?

Option 1 (recommended): at deploy time. Ansible runs on the developer's machine with that developer's AWS profile, reads the workspace's secret from Secrets Manager, and writes the server's .env (mode 0600). The server never needs AWS credentials to read secrets, and the app keeps reading .env as it does now. The trade-off: changing a secret takes a deploy (or rerunning the task that writes .env) before the app sees it.

Option 2: at run time. Django's settings fetch the secret from Secrets Manager with boto3 when the app starts. A secret change takes only a restart. The trade-off: Lightsail instances can't use IAM instance profiles, so the server needs a long-lived IAM access key in .env just to read the other secrets, which leaves a secret on disk anyway and adds an AWS call to every startup, including manage.py commands.

Which option should we use? Answer by closing this bead with the choice as the close reason.

title: Fix the Ansible task that installs uv
description: The Ansible task that installs uv (infra/ansible/tasks/install/uv.yml) runs `curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh` with ansible.builtin.command. The command module does not run a shell, so the pipe is passed to curl as arguments and uv is never installed. Server initialization fails at this task, and uv has to be installed by hand on the server. Switch the task to ansible.builtin.shell so the pipe works. Keep become: false so uv installs into the ubuntu user's ~/.local/bin, where the deploy tasks expect it, and keep the creates guard so reruns skip it.
acceptance_criteria:
- The task uses ansible.builtin.shell, still runs as the ubuntu user, and keeps the creates guard.
- just infra-all passes (ansible-lint may need its noqa comment updated for the shell module).
- Running the init playbook on a server without uv installs it at ~/.local/bin/uv.

title: Give EmailTransfer a UUID and a short slug
description: Following the UUID convention in docs/design.md (shared bead tools-z53.9): EmailTransfer extends common.models.SlugModel with slug_prefix T, so its ID is a UUID and its slug looks like T3f2a9c1e instead of T000001. Remove its own slug field and save override. Nothing is deployed, so replace the ETS's migrations with one fresh initial migration.
acceptance_criteria: Tests first: the slug is T plus the first 8 hex characters of the UUID; it doesn't change on later saves; a colliding slug gets a new UUID and slug; history still records changes. README updated. just ci passes.
close_reason: EmailTransfer extends SlugModel with prefix T; its slug is now T + 8 hex chars of its UUID. Tests cover the slug format, stability across saves, collision retry, and history. Replaced the ETS migrations with a fresh 0001 (nothing deployed).

title: Use UUID primary keys for every model
description:
Decision (Liam, 2026-10-15): every ClinGen Tools model uses a UUID primary key instead of an auto-incrementing integer, so data from the standalone AS and CSS can move into the shared database without ID clashes, and IDs aren't guessable. Models with a human-readable slug use a type letter plus the first 8 hex characters of the UUID (like a short Git hash), such as T3f2a9c1e; on the rare collision, the model picks a new UUID. This replaces the HCI's zero-padded integer slugs (T000001) on purpose.

Add to the common app: an abstract UUIDModel (UUID primary key) and an abstract SlugModel (UUIDModel plus a unique slug built from a per-model prefix). UserProfile extends UUIDModel. Set SIMPLE_HISTORY_HISTORY_ID_USE_UUID so history rows use UUIDs too. Django's own models (User, sessions, admin log) keep their integer IDs. Nothing is deployed, so regenerate auth_'s initial migration instead of converting; developers reset their local tools.db. Document the convention in docs/design.md and AGENTS.md.
acceptance_criteria: Tests first: UUIDModel gives a UUID primary key; SlugModel builds prefix + 8 hex chars, keeps the slug on later saves, and picks a new UUID when the slug is taken; UserProfile and its history rows have UUID IDs. READMEs, docs/design.md, and AGENTS.md updated. just ci passes.
close_reason: Added common.models.UUIDModel and SlugModel (prefix + first 8 hex chars, new UUID on collision), moved UserProfile to UUIDModel, set SIMPLE_HISTORY_HISTORY_ID_USE_UUID, and regenerated auth_'s initial migration (nothing deployed). The history-ID setting also needed an ETS migration here. SlugModel's save and collision retry are tested through EmailTransfer in the next bead, since it's the first concrete slug model. Documented in docs/design.md and AGENTS.md.

title: Navigate the ETS with tabs
description: Liam's feedback: the ETS uses buttons to move between its pages, which looks odd. Use Bulma's boxed tabs (tabs is-boxed) for New Transfer and Past Transfers instead, with the current page's tab active (a transfer's page counts as Past Transfers). Every ETS page keeps the title and subtitle above the tabs.

title: Use plain language in the ETS's pages
description:
Liam's feedback after trying the preview: ETS users aren't technical, so every page (the preview, the precondition failures, the flash messages, the transfer list and detail pages, the dry-run banner) should describe a transfer in plain language. Say 'sign-in account' for the Cognito user and 'GCI/VCI profile' for the DynamoDB user record, and never show PKs, Cognito usernames, attribute names like user_status, or raw AWS errors.

The technical details still have to be saved for developers: each step keeps its technical description and any raw error, and EmailTransfer saves the old and new Cognito usernames, the old record's PK, and the retired record's PK, if there was one. They're visible in the Django admin, not on the ETS's pages. Technical failures and AWS errors are also logged, so Sentry sees them.
acceptance_criteria: Tests first: step summaries and precondition failures name no PKs, usernames, or attribute names; the technical descriptions still do; a transfer saves the usernames and PKs; a failed step saves the raw error on the record but the detail page doesn't show it; AWS errors flash a plain message. README and docs/design.md updated if needed. just ci passes.
close_reason: Steps now have a plain summary (shown) and a technical description (saved). Precondition failures, the dry-run banner, status tags, and error messages are plain; AWS errors and the active-record case are logged. EmailTransfer saves the Cognito usernames and the moved and retired record PKs; each step saves its raw error.

title: Replace Sentry's deprecated send_default_pii with data_collection
description: sentry-sdk 2.72 deprecates the send_default_pii option in favor of data_collection, and every test run prints a DeprecationWarning from sentry_sdk.init() in src/config/settings/base.py. The HCI uses the same setting, so decide what we want Sentry to collect (user info, request bodies, and so on) and set data_collection explicitly instead of carrying over send_default_pii=True. See the docstring for data_collection in sentry_sdk/consts.py and https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/python/configuration/options/#data_collection.

title: Connect the ETS to real AWS on tools-test and prod
description:
Once the AWS-access decision is made, give the deployed ETS real credentials and try it.

- Create the ETS's IAM user in the account the decision names, with only the permissions docs/design.md lists. Whether it's managed in infra/terraform depends on the decision.

title: Run a confirmed transfer and record each step
description:
Add the second half: when staff confirm a preview, run the transfer.

- Re-check the preconditions at confirm time, since the data may have changed since the preview.
- Save an EmailTransfer (status pending) before the first change, then run the steps in order: retire the requested-activation record if present, update the old record's email, disable the old Cognito user, enable the new one (skip if already enabled). Record each step's result on the EmailTransfer as it finishes.
- On the first failure, stop, mark the transfer failed, and store the error. Don't try to undo earlier steps.
- Show a detail page for the transfer with each step's result, and a list page of past transfers (django-tables2 if it's already ported, a plain table template otherwise).
acceptance_criteria:
- Tests for a full success, for the requested-activation path, and for a failure at each step (the later steps don't run, and the record shows which steps finished).
- A test that preconditions are re-checked on confirm.
- History records who ran each transfer.
- No test reaches AWS. just ci passes; docs/design.md updated if behavior changed.
notes: Include the ETS_DRY_RUN mode from the epic's notes: with it on, write steps are recorded as skipped (dry run) and none of the AWS write calls are made. Tests cover a dry run making no write calls.

Added list and detail pages with plain tables (django-tables2 isn't ported).

title: Check preconditions and preview a transfer
description:
Add the first half of the transfer flow: staff enter the old and new emails, and the ETS checks the preconditions and shows what it would change, without changing anything.

- A form with old_email and new_email (both required, valid emails, and not equal).
- A preconditions function that uses clients.py and returns either a list of failures or the plan. Preconditions are listed in docs/design.md: old email has a Cognito user and a DynamoDB record; new email has a Cognito user; new email has no DynamoDB record or one with user_status 'requested activation'.
- The plan lists the steps that will run, with Cognito usernames and DynamoDB PKs, and notes when the new user is already enabled (that step is skipped).
- If a precondition fails, show every failure and no confirm button. Use flash messages only for errors, per the HCI convention.

- View tests: invalid form, failed preconditions (no confirm button), and a valid preview that lists the steps.
- No test reaches AWS. just ci passes.

title: Add the ETS app, AWS client, and EmailTransfer model
description:
Create src/email_transfer_service/ and mount it at /ets/ (namespace ets) so it appears on the landing page.

- clients.py: a small wrapper around boto3 with functions for the calls the script makes: find a Cognito user by email (list_users with an email filter), find a DynamoDB user record by email (query item_type_index for item_type 'user', filtered by email, following LastEvaluatedKey), retire a record, update a record's email, and disable or enable a Cognito user. Settings come from env vars (add them to .env.example with dummy values): ETS_AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, ETS_AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, ETS_AWS_REGION, ETS_COGNITO_USER_POOL_ID, ETS_DYNAMODB_TABLE_NAME. The decision bead on AWS access may rename these.
- models.py: EmailTransfer with old_email, new_email, the user who ran it, a status (pending, succeeded, failed), per-step results, an error message, and timestamps. Zero-padded slug like other ClinGen apps (T000001). django-simple-history on.
- A placeholder index view at /ets/ protected by has_ets_permissions.
- Add boto3 (and boto3-stubs for Cognito and DynamoDB if ty needs them).
acceptance_criteria:
- Tests for each client function using botocore Stubber, including DynamoDB pagination and the not-found cases.
- Model tests: slug generation and history.
- View tests: /ets/ returns 403 without has_ets_permissions and 200 with it; the landing page lists the ETS.
- just ci passes; README and docs.json updated.
close_reason: Added the email_transfer_service app at /ets/, EtsClient (boto3 low-level clients so Stubber covers every call), EmailTransfer with a dry_run flag, and a permission-gated index. Core's landing-page tests now build their URLconfs from the project's minus its tools.

title: Build the Email Transfer Service
description: Build the ETS at /ets/: a staff-facing form that moves a GCI or VCI user's account from an old email to a new one, replacing the hand-run update_email.py script. docs/design.md ('The Email Transfer Service') describes the behavior.
design:
Decisions:
- The behavior matches the update_email.py script: the same preconditions and the same four steps in the same order (retire a 'requested activation' record for the new email if there is one, point the old record at the new email, disable the old Cognito user, enable the new one). docs/design.md lists them.
- There is no override. The script's --force flag has no equivalent; a transfer that fails the preconditions needs a developer.
- Only users with UserProfile.has_ets_permissions can use the ETS (the shared epic adds the flag and mixin).
- Cognito and DynamoDB can't be changed atomically. An EmailTransfer record is saved before the first change, and each step's result is recorded as it runs. The run stops at the first failure.
- AWS settings (credentials, region, user pool ID, table name) come from the environment, never code. Tests never reach AWS: use botocore's Stubber.
- The Django app is src/email_transfer_service/, mounted at /ets/ with namespace ets.
- Where the AWS access comes from is undecided; see the decision bead that blocks wiring up real AWS.
notes:
Decision (Liam, 2026-10-14): get the ETS working locally first, doing dry runs only. ETS_DRY_RUN makes a confirmed transfer run the lookups and record every step, but skip the AWS writes; each write step is recorded as skipped (dry run) and the EmailTransfer has dry_run=True. Pages show a dry-run banner while it's on. tools-eap.4 turns it off on the servers once AWS access is decided. Locally, the ETS_ AWS vars point at the same account the update_email.py script uses, read-only in practice because dry run is on.

Update (Liam, 2026-10-15): ETS_DRY_RUN turns off only when it's exactly 0, matching the HCI's RUN_CONTRACT_TESTS=1 convention (0/1 flags across Liam's projects). Anything else, including empty, keeps dry run on.

title: Provision and deploy prod
description:
Repeat the tools-test bead for production at https://tools.clinicalgenome.org: terraform workspace new prod, the prod SSH key (~/.ssh/tools_ansible_prod_ed25519), the prod inventory entry, the prod .env, just server-prod-init, and just server-prod-deploy. The user runs the steps that create AWS resources.

Also record the backup reader credentials (backup_reader_* outputs, prod only) somewhere the team keeps secrets; the restore check that uses them is out of scope here. File follow-up beads for a CD workflow and uptime monitoring rather than doing them here.

- https://tools.clinicalgenome.org serves the landing page over HTTPS, and Clerk sign-in works.
- just server-prod-deploy succeeds and prints a pre-deployment backup name.
- Follow-up beads exist for CD and uptime monitoring.

title: Provision and deploy tools-test
description:
Create the test infrastructure and deploy the app to https://tools-test.clinicalgenome.org. The user runs every step that creates AWS resources; the agent prepares commands, checks results, and fixes infra/ code when something fails.

Steps (docs/how-to.md has the details):
1. Prerequisite: main is pushed to https://github.com/ClinGen/tools (the user does this).
2. Create the tools_terraform_lock DynamoDB table (first time only).
3. Create ~/.ssh/tools_ansible_test_ed25519.
4. In infra/terraform: terraform init, terraform workspace new test, terraform apply. Commit .terraform.lock.hcl.
5. Copy infra/ansible/inventory.example.ini to inventory.ini and fill in the test IP.
6. Create the server's .env from .env.example: production settings, Clerk keys from the shared Clerk application, Sentry, and the backup credentials from terraform output (How to Configure Backup Credentials).
7. just server-test-init, then just server-test-deploy to confirm the pre-migration backup works.

Fix anything in infra/ or docs/how-to.md that turns out to be wrong along the way.
acceptance_criteria:
- https://tools-test.clinicalgenome.org serves the landing page over HTTPS.
- Signing in with Clerk works on tools-test.
- just server-test-deploy succeeds and prints a pre-deployment backup name, and manage.py listbackups on the server shows it.
- Requests for blocked paths (for example /.env) return 403.
- docs/how-to.md matches what was actually done, and just infra-all passes.

title: Add Sentry and S3 database backups
description:
Wire up Sentry and django-dbbackup so the deploy playbook's pre-migration backup works.

- Sentry: initialize in settings/base.py as hla-curation-interface/src/config/settings/base.py does, reading SENTRY_DSN and SENTRY_ENV. Tag every event with the tool that handled the request, taken from the resolved URL's namespace (as, css, ets, or none for the landing page), as docs/design.md describes.
- django-dbbackup: add the dependency and storage settings as the HCI does, reading DBBACKUP_BUCKET_NAME, AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, and AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY. Backups are compressed and named with SUBDOMAIN.
- Add every new variable to .env.example.
- infra/ansible/tasks/admin/django_dbbackup_predeploy.yml is already in place; confirm the command it runs works locally against a local filesystem storage in dev.
acceptance_criteria:
- A test checks that the tool tag is set from the URL namespace for a tool URL and is absent for /.
- A test checks that the dbbackup storage is configured from the environment variables.
- uv run src/manage.py dbbackup works in dev against local storage.
- just ci passes; .env.example and the src/config README are updated.
close_reason: Sentry init ported from the HCI, plus ToolTagMiddleware, which tags events with the tool's URL namespace (only for known tools). dbbackup and S3 storage ported from the HCI; local backups go to backups/. Verified manage.py dbbackup -o pre-deployment/... works locally, the same command the deploy runs. Kept send_default_pii for parity with the HCI and filed a chore to move to data_collection.

title: Add Clerk sign-in and per-tool permissions
description:
Port src/auth_ from hla-curation-interface/src/auth_ so staff sign in with Clerk, and add per-tool permissions.

- Port the ClerkBackend, UserProfile, sign-in and sign-out views, templates, and the Clerk JS. Drop HCI-only fields and checks (PHI agreement, curation and review permissions).
- UserProfile gets has_ets_permissions (BooleanField, default False). Later tools add their own flag the same way.
- auth_/permissions.py: a mixin and a decorator that take the name of a tool's flag, require a signed-in user, and return 403 if the flag isn't set. Example: ToolPermissionMixin with tool_permission = 'has_ets_permissions'.
- Register UserProfile in the Django admin so staff can grant the flag. Keep django-simple-history on UserProfile so grants are audited.
- Settings read CLERK_SECRET_KEY and CLERK_PUBLISHABLE_KEY from the environment; add them to .env.example. The Clerk application is shared with other ClinGen apps (see the epic design).
- The landing page stays public; tools' pages are protected.
- Update the Authentication section of docs/design.md if the port differs from it.
acceptance_criteria:
- Port the HCI's auth_ tests that still apply, and add tests that: an anonymous user is redirected to sign-in from a protected view; a signed-in user without has_ets_permissions gets 403; a signed-in user with it gets 200; the landing page works for an anonymous user.
- Tests mock Clerk; none call Clerk's servers.
- just ci passes. src/auth_/README.md exists and docs.json lists it.
notes: Reworked to copy the HCI's Clerk sign-in as closely as possible, at the user's request: HCI views, JSX (hard-coded /auth/callback), templates, backend, navbar buttons, GET logout, profile page, os.environ for the Clerk keys, LOGIN_URL=/auth/login. Dropped the earlier next-URL handling, POST-only logout, and prod Clerk-key check.
close_reason: Ported Clerk sign-in from the HCI without PHI and curation permissions. UserProfile has has_ets_permissions; ToolPermissionMixin and tool_permission_required check a flag by name (an unknown name raises ImproperlyConfigured). Changes from the HCI: callback URL passed to the JS instead of hard-coded, login remembers a local next URL, logout is POST-only, prod refuses to start without the Clerk keys. Large diff (~1100 lines) kept as one PR because sign-in and permissions depend on each other.

title: Add the landing page and base layout
description:
Add the page at / that links to each tool, plus the shared layout every tool's pages extend.

- src/core/: an app with a landing page view and template. The page lists each tool (AS at /as/, CSS at /css/, ETS at /ets/) with its one-line description from README.md. List only tools whose URLconf is mounted, so the page never links to a 404; until the ETS exists, the page may list no tools and should say so.
- src/templates/: base.html (Bulma, HTMX, a header with the site name, a footer) and error pages 403, 404, and 500. Adapt from clinvar-submission-service/src/templates.
- src/static/ and build.js: vendor Bulma, HTMX, and bootstrap-icons as the CSS does.
- src/common/: only what this bead needs (for example, context processors). Port more of common later, when a tool needs it.
- WhiteNoise serves static files. Build URLs with {% url %}, never hard-coded paths.
- Add src/core, src/common, src/templates, and src/static to docs.json and scaffold their READMEs.
acceptance_criteria:
- Tests in src/core/tests.py: GET / returns 200 and renders the base layout; a mounted tool appears with a link built by reverse(); an unmounted tool does not appear; the empty state shows when no tools are mounted.
- Tests that the 404 and 500 handlers render their templates.
- just django-collectstatic and just ci pass.
- READMEs for every new directory, and docs.json updated.

The 500 page has no contact email because the team has no shared address yet. Fixed HTMX CSRF header name (X-CSRFToken; the CSS's X-CSRF-TOKEN isn't one Django reads).

title: Add the Django project skeleton
description:
Create the Django project in src/ so that just ci passes on an empty project.

- pyproject.toml modeled on clinvar-submission-service/pyproject.toml: project name clinvar-submission-service -> tools, same Ruff, coverage, pytest, and django-stubs config. Add django-dbbackup later (separate bead), not here.
- src/manage.py and src/config/ (urls.py, wsgi.py, settings/base.py, dev.py, test.py, prod.py) adapted from the CSS. Settings read SECRET_KEY, ENV, ALLOWED_HOSTS, and similar from the environment.
- .env.example at the root listing every variable the settings read, with dummy values.
- package.json, build.js, and biome.json adapted from the CSS so js-build and js-lint work.
- docs.json lists src/config, and src/config/README.md is scaffolded with uv run docs.py generate --directory src/config.
- README.md Getting Started: copy .env.example to .env.

- A test in src/config/tests.py checks that the test settings load and that Django's system check passes.
- uv sync, npm ci, and just ci all pass.

title: Stand up ClinGen Tools on tools-test and prod
description: Build the shared Django project that every tool runs in, and deploy it to tools-test.clinicalgenome.org and then tools.clinicalgenome.org. When this epic is done, the landing page is live, staff can sign in with Clerk, and the ETS epic can start.
design:
docs/design.md describes the architecture; this epic builds its shared parts.

Decisions:
- Base the skeleton on the CSS (clinvar-submission-service/src: config, core, common, templates, static) and port auth_ from the HCI (hla-curation-interface/src/auth_), which already uses Clerk. Adapt, don't copy blindly: drop HCI-only concepts such as the PHI agreement and curation permissions.
- Staff sign in with Clerk. We share an existing ClinGen Clerk application with other apps rather than creating a new one, so the Clerk keys come from that application. Keys live only in .env files, never in code or beads.
- Permissions are per tool. UserProfile gets one boolean flag per tool (starting with ETS), and each tool's views check their own flag through a mixin in auth_. Staff grant flags in the Django admin.
- Infrastructure is already written in infra/ (Terraform and Ansible, copied from the HCI). Beads here may fix it but shouldn't redesign it.
- The repo is public at https://github.com/ClinGen/tools, so the server clones over HTTPS. The server can only deploy what has been pushed to main; pushing is the user's call.
- The user runs terraform apply and anything else that creates billed AWS resources. Agents prepare the commands and stop.

title: Decide where the ETS gets its AWS access
description:
The ETS changes GCI and VCI user accounts in an AWS Cognito user pool and the GeneVariantCuration DynamoDB table (see 'The Email Transfer Service' in docs/design.md). Before we can build or deploy it, we need answers to these questions:

1. Which AWS account holds the GCI/VCI Cognito user pool and the GeneVariantCuration table?
2. Who creates the ETS's IAM user in that account, and is it managed by Terraform in this repo or elsewhere? The design calls for least privilege: list, enable, and disable users in the one user pool, and query and update items in the one table.
3. Does the ETS on tools-test need to reach a test user pool and table, so we can try transfers without touching production data? If so, which ones?
4. What are the names of the environment variables for the credentials, region, user pool ID, and table name, and where are the values kept?

The ETS reads all of these from the environment, never from code.

title: Accept and store a record's citations
description: ClinVar's germlineClassification takes a citation list (PubMed, BookShelf, DOI, or pmc IDs, or URLs). The CSS's content schema forbids fields it doesn't model, so today a client can't send citations. Add a Citation model (a record's db, ID, or URL), accept germlineClassification.citation in content.Content, and save the citations with the record.
acceptance_criteria: Tests: a record's citations are saved in order; a citation with both an ID and a URL gets 422; the fixture gains a cited record and still matches its payload. just ci passes.

title: Add about, contact, and help pages
description: The core app has only the landing page. Add about, contact, and help pages to core, linked from the footer or navbar, following the HCI and the AS's pages: about says what ClinGen Tools is, contact gives the team's contact address, and help points staff to where to get help with each tool. Also show the contact address on the 500 page. Use plain language: these pages are for non-technical staff.
acceptance_criteria: Tests in src/core/tests.py check each page renders in the base layout with its title, and the 500 page shows the contact address. src/core/README.md and src/templates/README.md describe the new templates. just ci passes.

title: Add CI, Codecov, and GitHub templates
description: The repo has no .github/ directory, so nothing checks a pull request. Add a GitHub Actions workflow that runs each check just ci runs as its own job (Python and JavaScript formatting and linting, the ty type check, the Django check, and the tests), a workflow that uploads test coverage to Codecov, a codecov.yml, the HCI's issue templates (bug, critical, feature, improvement) and pull request template, local composite actions that install the Python and JavaScript dependencies, and gh-actions recipes in the justfile. Follow the HCI's .github/ setup. Add .github to docs.json with a README.
acceptance_criteria: CI runs every check in just ci as a separate job on pull requests to main; coverage uploads to Codecov; .github/README.md describes each file; just ci passes.
